title: CI/CD Platform
description: Same task, same box, on your laptop and in any CI. The whole picture and a guide to build your own.

ideas.title: Three ideas. The rest is detail.

items.title: Tasks do the work.
items.text: Every check and build is a named task. It runs in a container, the same box on your laptop and on any runner. Common tasks are written once and shared: use them as they are, tweak them or write your own.
items.code:
ci/node/build:
  image: ci/node
  run: npm run build
items.why: one build, not one for you and one for CI

items.title: Workflows only route.
items.text: A workflow listens for events and calls tasks by name. It never installs a toolchain or runs a build itself. Routing and execution are different jobs, and they stay apart.

items.title: Delivery isn't yours to rewrite.
items.text: Deploy, apply and publish own the credentials and how they run. A project only passes inputs, like a domain or a bucket.
items.code:
deliver: static-site
domain: example.com
bucket: my-site
items.why: every release goes the same way

picture.title: Two callers, one box.
picture.lede: Everything from the first call to the release, on one sheet. Pick any part to look closer.
picture.swipe: Swipe to see the whole scheme

scene.label: The whole scheme: a laptop calls one task by name, a runner runs a workflow of task names. Each CI task joins its shared task in the project's tasks and runs in the box. The result and the cache stay outside the box, and the cache outlives every run. Deploy is a project task without a shared one: it runs past the box, through the gate to delivery, which only takes inputs.

route.title: Route
route.note: a laptop calls a task, a runner a workflow

run.title: Run
run.note: tasks do the work, in the box

legend.text: Laptop: you call one task by name.
Runner: an event starts the workflow.
Shared task: common logic any project can reuse.

parts.label: Laptop
parts.text: Run the CI tasks **before you push**: `lint`, `test`, `build`, right on your machine.

points.title: Nothing to set up
points.text: No tools to install, no versions to match. The box brings them.

points.title: Breaks here first
points.text: A broken build shows up on your machine, not later in a CI log.

parts.label: Runner
parts.text: An event starts the **whole workflow** on a runner: `lint`, `test`, `build`, then `deploy`.

points.title: A bare runner is enough
points.text: Docker-in-Docker, nothing else. No toolchains to install or keep up to date on CI machines.

points.title: Privileges under control
points.text: You decide what each task container may do, down to dropping every capability.

points.title: No surprises after a push
points.text: These are the tasks you already ran on your laptop. Green there means green here.

parts.label: Project tasks
parts.text: The project's **own task list**: names, arguments and versions are decided here, not in CI config.

points.title: Shared blocks, your way
points.text: Use a shared task as it is, pass it your own arguments or run your own command in its image.

points.title: Project quirks welcome
points.text: Anything only this project needs becomes a task of its own, right next to the shared ones.

points.title: Updates when you say so
points.text: A change in a shared task reaches your project only when you choose to take it.

parts.label: Shared tasks
parts.text: **How to run a tool**, written once: the image, the mounts, the cache and the flags.

points.title: No copy-paste between repos
points.text: Projects call the shared task instead of carrying the same container commands around.

points.title: One fix reaches everyone
points.text: Tune a flag or add a cache once, and every project using it gets the change on its next update.

points.title: Defaults you can override
points.text: Version, arguments, env and container settings come preset. A project changes what it needs; the safety flags stay put.

parts.label: Images
parts.text: **The tools themselves**, packed into images and tagged by tool version: `node:22.23.1`, `golang:1.27.1`, `terraform:1.15.9`.

points.title: The tag tells the truth
points.text: It is the tool's version, and there is no latest. You always know what you are running.

parts.label: The box
parts.text: A **fresh container** for every run: tools from the image, your code mounted in.

points.title: Clean every time
points.text: Nothing leaks in from the last run or from your machine. If it passes here, it isn't luck.

points.title: In and out on purpose
points.text: Folders, env, ports and the user are part of the task's setup. Nothing crosses the walls unless the task lets it.

points.title: Fast reruns
points.text: Caches live outside and are mounted in. Nothing gets downloaded twice.

parts.label: The gate
parts.text: **One checkpoint** between CI and CD: delivery starts only when every task before it is green.

points.title: One required check
points.text: Protect the branch with the gate alone. Add or rename tasks, and the rule keeps working.

points.title: When and whether
points.text: The workflow decides when delivery runs. The gate decides whether it may.

points.title: Exceptions on purpose
points.text: Mark the jobs that may be skipped or ignored. Everything else has to pass.

parts.label: Delivery
parts.text: **Deploy, apply and publish** come ready-made. A project fills in its inputs and calls them.

points.title: Ships on day one
points.text: A new project sets a few inputs and releases like the rest. No release scripts to write or review.

points.title: Every release looks the same
points.text: One way out for every project. When something breaks, it breaks in a place you already know.

divider.text: Want one of your own? The details are below

bends.title: Three things stay. Everything else bends.

stays.label: Stays
items: Tasks do the work, in a container.
Workflows call names and nothing else.

bend.label: Bends
items: Any CI that runs a shell and starts containers.
Docker or Podman as the engine: one setting in the runner.
A shared task as it is, with your vars, your own command in its image, or a task of your own.
Ready-made workflow presets, or your own workflows built from the same blocks.
Delivery as a workflow preset or as a task no project can include.
My images and modules, or yours. Caches wherever you point them.

headline: The guide
guide.title: The guide: build your own
guide.intro: The concept doesn't care which tools you pick. This guide does: it's written for Taskfile and GitHub Actions, the pair I run myself. Most steps end with a check you can run before moving on.

brief.label: Tasks
brief.text: I run tasks with [Taskfile](https://taskfile.dev). It already has what this setup leans on:
points: [Remote includes](https://taskfile.dev/docs/remote-taskfiles) fetch shared Taskfiles straight from a repo, pinned to a commit.
[Vars](https://taskfile.dev/docs/guide/includes#vars-of-included-taskfiles) and [env](https://taskfile.dev/docs/guide/environment) let each project tune what it brings in.
[Internal tasks](https://taskfile.dev/docs/guide/defining-tasks#internal-tasks) keep the helpers out of the task list.
brief.aside: The same idea works with [just](https://just.systems) or [Make](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/) too, but you'll write more glue: neither can fetch shared files from a repo.

brief.label: CI
brief.text: The CI part of the guide is written for [GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/actions), because that's where my code lives. The process itself runs just as well on [GitLab CI](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/), [Gitea Actions](https://docs.gitea.com/usage/actions/overview), [Jenkins](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/) or any CI that has a shell and can start containers.
brief.punch: Only the files that call the tasks change. The images and the tasks stay as they are.

brief.label: Before you start
points: a registry you can push images to
a git repo for the shared Taskfiles
a CI whose runners can run Docker-in-Docker

brief.label: Shortcut
brief.text: Rather not build it all yourself? Take mine: [images](https://github.com/mr-chelyshkin/images), [tasks](https://github.com/mr-chelyshkin/tasks) and [actions](https://github.com/mr-chelyshkin/actions).
brief.aside: This site runs on them too: here are its [Taskfile](https://github.com/mr-chelyshkin/site/blob/main/Taskfile.yml) and [workflows](https://github.com/mr-chelyshkin/site/tree/main/.github/workflows).

steps.title: Pack the tools
steps.why: Every tool lives in an image, at a pinned version. Nobody installs a toolchain by hand.
actions: Build it for every platform your laptops and runners use.
Push it to your registry under a version tag, not `latest`.

code.label: Build and publish
code.code:
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  --build-arg NODE_VERSION=22.23.1 \
  --tag your-registry/node:22.23.1 --push tools/node

steps.check: `docker run --rm your-registry/node:22.23.1 node --version` prints the version you pinned.

steps.title: Teach the run
steps.why: One shared task starts every container. Tool modules decide what runs in it, projects only change the settings.

items.name: Project
items.text: names the work and holds the settings

items.name: Module
items.text: decides what runs: the image, the cache

items.name: Runner
items.text: decides how it starts: the safety flags

actions: Write the runner: one `run` task. It fixes the safe part (no root, no capabilities, the project at `/workspace`, the cache on the host) and takes the rest as settings with defaults.
Build a module per tool on top: it picks the image and the cache, then calls the runner, included as `internal`.
Grow `run` and a read-only `audit` from `exec`. Pass `TASK_CONTEXT` down at each hop: that's how a project's settings reach the runner.
Tag a release. Projects pin its commit.

code.label: shared-tasks/docker/Taskfile.yml
shared-tasks/node/Taskfile.yml
code.code:
version: '3'

includes:
  docker:
    taskfile: ../docker/Taskfile.yml
    internal: true # projects never call the runner directly

tasks:
  exec:
    requires:
      vars: [CMD]
    vars:
      context:
        ref: '.TASK_CONTEXT | default .'
      version: '{{.context.NODE_VERSION | default "22.23.1"}}'
    cmds:
      # what to run is decided here, how to run it in the runner
      - task: docker:run
        vars:
          IMAGE: 'your-registry/node:{{.version}}'
          CMD: '{{.CMD}}'
          PROJECT_ROOT: '{{.context.PROJECT_ROOT | default .ROOT_DIR}}'
          WORKDIR: '{{.context.NODE_DIR | default "."}}'
          CACHE_DIR: .cache/node
          CACHE_TARGET: /tmp/node-cache
          ENVS: [NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/tmp/node-cache]
          # the project's settings travel down with the call
          TASK_CONTEXT:
            ref: .context

  # an npm script, built on exec
  run:
    requires:
      vars: [SCRIPT]
    cmds:
      - task: exec
        vars:
          CMD: sh -c 'npm ci && npm run {{.SCRIPT}}'
          TASK_CONTEXT:
            ref: '.TASK_CONTEXT | default .'

  # read-only, whatever the project set
  audit:
    cmds:
      - task: exec
        vars:
          CMD: npm audit --audit-level=high
          TASK_CONTEXT:
            ref: 'merge (dict "CONTAINER_MOUNT_MODE" "ro") (.TASK_CONTEXT | default .)'

steps.title: Name the work
steps.why: The project decides what each name does. CI only ever sees the names.
actions: Include the module, pinned to a commit. Its `vars` apply to every call from the project.
Add a `ci/<area>/<verb>` task for everything CI should run: build, test, lint.
Use a shared task as is, give it an argument, or run your own command. A setting passed with one call stays with that call.

code.label: Taskfile.yml, in the project
code.code:
version: '3'

includes:
  node:
    taskfile: https://your-git/shared-tasks/raw/<commit>/node/Taskfile.yml
    vars: # for every call from this project
      NODE_VERSION: '22.23.1'
      NODE_DIR: app
      CONTAINER_ENVS: NPM_TOKEN

tasks:
  ci/node/build: # a shared task with an argument
    cmds:
      - task: node:run
        vars: { SCRIPT: build }

  ci/node/audit: # a shared task as is
    cmds:
      - task: node:audit

  run/dev: # your own command, a setting for this call only
    cmds:
      - task: node:exec
        vars:
          CMD: sh -c 'npm ci && npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0'
          CONTAINER_PORTS: 127.0.0.1:5173:5173

steps.title: Call it from CI
steps.why: CI gets one thin wrapper: it installs Task and runs a task by name. The job passes the name and its arguments, nothing else.
actions: Give your runners Docker-in-Docker: the tasks start their containers there.
Write the wrapper once: install Task at a pinned version, check its checksum, keep it cached, run the task.
Give it two inputs: the task name and its arguments, one per line. Arguments reach Task as data, never through a shell.
Call it once per check, then add a last job that passes only when all of them passed.

code.label: .github/workflows/pr.yml
code.code:
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: mr-chelyshkin/actions/task-run@v2
        with:
          task: ci/node/build # a name from the project's Taskfile
          args: | # optional, one per line, passed as data
            KEY=value

  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: mr-chelyshkin/actions/task-run@v2
        with:
          task: ci/node/audit

  gate: # passes only when every check passed
    if: always()
    needs: [build, audit]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: mr-chelyshkin/actions/job-results-check@v2
        with:
          results: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

code.label: The same wrapper in other CIs: a sketch
code.code:
# GitLab CI: a job template from a shared repo
include:
  - project: your-group/ci-templates
    ref: <commit>
    file: task-run.yml

build:
  extends: .task-run
  variables:
    TASK_NAME: ci/node/build
    TASK_ARGS: KEY=value

# Jenkins: a step from a shared library
@Library('ci-templates@<commit>') _
taskRun(name: 'ci/node/build', args: ['KEY=value'])

steps.check: A pull request runs the same `ci/node/build` as your laptop and gets the same result.

steps.title: Keep the deploy separate
steps.why: Delivery is written once, outside the projects. A project fills in the settings and never touches the steps.
actions: Write the deploy once: as a ready-made pipeline step, or as a task projects can't include.
Take settings only: names, regions, buckets. No commands.
Run it after all checks pass, on tags or the main branch, with short-lived keys.
steps.check: Your laptop can run every `ci/*` task and none of the deploy steps.

code.label: .github/workflows/publish.yml

items.q: Why not put the build in the workflow?
items.a: Then it only runs in CI. A task runs the same on your laptop, and a new CI doesn't mean a new build.

items.q: Can a project write its own tasks?
items.a: Sure. Use a shared task as is, pass it vars, run your own command through `exec`, or write one from scratch. CI only sees the name.
In a folder of the project, mounted into the container. The container starts clean every time, the cache doesn't. On CI, its own cache keeps that folder between runs.

items.q: Does the runner need privileged Docker?
items.a: Yes, for Docker-in-Docker: without it the tasks have nowhere to start their containers. Keep the privileges with the daemon. Task containers drop every capability, can't gain new ones and run as your user. If a task truly needs a capability, add that one on its call, never `--privileged`.
It passes inputs: names, regions, buckets. The steps stay fixed: a workflow preset after the gate, or a locked task no project can include.
Same image, same mounts, same flags. The CPU may differ, which is why the images are built for amd64 and arm64.
